extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: A training environment for software engineering agents and verifiers containing real-world Python task instances from GitHub issues, with executable runtime environments, unit tests, and natural-language task descriptions. The paper also releases SWE-Gym Raw and SWE-Gym Lite.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 267)
extraction.citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym was constructed from GitHub issues and pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories. The authors used SEART GitHub search to identify repositories, then used SWE-Bench’s instance extraction script to convert repositories into task instances. They semi-manually created executable environments, manually configured dependencies using repository files and documentation, and validated instances with SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script. Annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that SWE-Gym Raw instances contain code, issue descriptions, and the solution, but do not contain executable environments or a guarantee that unit tests are effective for evaluating correctness. Instances that failed environment setup or validation were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world GitHub issues, pull requests, repository snapshots, codebases, unit tests, CI scripts, documentation, and configuration files from 11 open-source Python repositories; SWE-Gym Raw additionally includes 64,689 Python GitHub issue instances from 358 repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Repositories were selected if created before July 1, 2022; the paper does not specify the exact dates of issue collection or environment construction beyond the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Instances were versioned using repository information such as pyproject.toml and git tags; dependencies were manually configured per task instance; gold patches were validated using execution-based validation; failed instances were filtered out; SWE-Gym Lite was created by applying the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline and excluding tasks requiring edits to more than one file, poorly described tasks, overly complex diffs, and tests focused on error-message validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Repositories were filtered to those created before July 1, 2022, with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors. For SWE-Gym Lite, tasks were filtered to easier, more self-contained instances. Instances that failed setup or validation were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper states that approximately 200 human annotation hours were required, and that annotations were done by a subset of the authors. The validation process used SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script to ensure the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SEART GitHub search; SWE-Bench instance extraction script; SWE-Bench execution-based validation script; Docker images were publicly released for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Gold patches were checked to ensure they passed more unit tests than the original code. The paper also discusses bias from repeated sampling toward easier tasks and introduces per-instance capping to mitigate this bias.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A subset of the authors performed the annotations; no further demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench instance extraction script, SWE-Bench execution-based validation script, OpenHands remote runtime, SGLang, torchtune, Unsloth
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that SWE-Gym, models, and agent trajectories are publicly released, and that pre-built Docker images are released for each instance. No versioning, update schedule, maintainers, or deprecation policy are specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No explicit collection of personal sensitive information is described. The dataset includes GitHub issue text and repository metadata; the paper does not state collection of attributes such as gender, age, language, or socio-economic status.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that improved automated software engineering could increase developer productivity and accessibility, support open-source infrastructure, and potentially affect software engineering jobs. It also notes possible misuse for malicious code generation and calls for responsible deployment considering security, safety, and economic impacts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a long-tail success distribution that biases training toward easier tasks when repeatedly sampling trajectories. It also discusses potential distribution bias from ignoring executable environments and from repository/task diversity, and introduces per-instance capping to mitigate easy-task bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by environment diversity, including the number of repositories, task types, and programming languages. The paper also notes that performance may be limited by compute budget for sampling trajectories, and that self-improvement results are modest. SWE-Gym Raw lacks executable environments and validated unit tests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering agents and verifiers; fine-tuning language models; inference-time scaling with verifiers; evaluation on SWE-Bench Lite and SWE-Bench Verified; rapid prototyping via SWE-Gym Lite.
